items.title: Delaware hit by rare November tornado
items.desc: Meanwhile, severe thunderstorms bring hailstones the size of baseballs in ArgentinaThe National Weather Service in the US has confirmed that an EF1 tornado touched down south-east of Newark in the Salem Woods neighbourhood, Delaware, on Thursday. The tornado reached 160 metres wide, had a path length of 4.4 miles (7.1km) and reached estimated peak winds of up to 100mph (161km/h). There were no injuries or fatalities but windows and roofs were damaged on several homes, a large hotel sign fell on to a number of cars, and a semi truck overturned on I95. Although Delaware often experiences a few tornadoes every year, this is only the second time the state has had tornado activity in November since 1950, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration. The only other November tornado recorded was in 1989.Severe storms have also resulted in tornadoes in Argentina as well as large hailstones. A round of severe thunderstorms moved through the central Córdoba province on Friday, bringing hailstones up to the size of a baseball (about 7.5cm in diameter). Parts of the province recorded up to 73mm of rainfall in just six hours early on Saturday. Such storms are common at this time of year. Water vapour from the Amazon meeting the Andes quickly condenses, resulting in massive cloud formations often associated with heavy downpours, lightning, tornadoes and large hailstones. items.title: Storm Charles causes floods and flight cancellations across southern Europe
items.desc: Heavy rain and strong winds have also caused disruption across British Columbia, Canada, over the last week Storm Charles has brought destructive weather to the Iberian peninsula this week, particularly in Portugal and the far south of Spain. Heavy rain and strong south-westerly winds arrived first in the Portuguese island of Madeira, before the system headed towards the mainland on 11 November. A wind gust of 84.5mph (136 km/h) was recorded at Funchal airport, alongside rainfall totals reaching 355mm (13.97in) in 12 hours. In Lisbon, 183 flights were cancelled on Wednesday, about a third of its normal daily traffic, while Madrid Barajas airport had 155 cancellations.After causing widespread flooding in Spain and Portugal, the system moved on a north-easterly track through southern France and then towards northern Italy. This resulted in significant flooding in parts of Cannes, some of which caused rock falls and led to the closure of roads along the French Riviera. The Italian weather service issued a red rainfall warning, its highest level, for the area extending from Tuscany to Venezia. items.title: November 17 blackout hoax: How a conspiracy theory went viral around the world
items.desc: A conspiracy theory claiming a worldwide “blackout” will hit on November 17 has spread across social media, cutting electricity, internet and banking services. The rumour stems from a routine US FEMA emergency alert test, but was amplified by cryptocurrency accounts, misleading claims about EU preparedness advice and references to The Simpsons. Recent technology outages, flight disruptions and cyberattacks have added to public anxiety, helping turn a routine test into a global blackout hoax.

items.title: Pope concludes South America homecoming, reassures faithful after cancer scare
items.desc: Pope Leo XIV finished Monday his 12-day tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru reiterating his advocacy for social justice, environmental protection and the importance of community. Just a month after undergoing lung cancer surgery, the 71-year-old pontiff drew millions of faithful across South America, where he spent nearly two decades as a missionary.

items.title: The new faces of the US Congress
items.desc: The United States Congress is about to welcome dozens of new faces. A majority of them, Democratic, after the "blue wave" in the midterm elections. FRANCE 24's Washington correspondent Fraser Jackson catches up with one of these new lawmakers as they go through orientation as they prepare to take office in January. He speaks with Katy Padilla Stout, U.S. Representative-elect for Texas's 23rd congressional district.

items.title: Should Ukraine trade Donbas for NATO membership?
items.desc: President Volodymyr Zelensky asserting that the United States has asked him about a straight-up swap Russia gets the Donbas, the rest of Ukraine gets NATO membership, a guarantee against Moscow later having a second go and annexing the entire country. Whether or not the offer’s real, serious or that either side would accept it. We’ll ask if the talk of partition signals some kind of turning point in a nearly five-year war that's also a brutal stalemate.

items.title: EU nations unveil Rwanda deal for migrant return hub
items.desc: Five EU countries including Germany and Denmark on Monday unveiled a deal to establish a migrant deportation centre in Rwanda -- the first such facility outside the bloc. The group, also comprising Austria, Greece and the Netherlands, has been gunning to open a "return-hub" despite rights groups' concerns, after the European Union cleared the way with a recent toughening of migration rules. FRANCE 24's Dave Keating reports from Brussels.

items.title: UEFA backs France's Diallo to stand against Infantino in FIFA election
items.desc: European football's governing body UEFA has given its "unanimous" backing to French Football Federation chief Philippe Diallo to stand against incumbent Gianni Infantino in March's FIFA presidential election, it said in a statement Monday. Under its Slovenian president Aleksander Ceferin, UEFA has led the opposition to Infantino since his announcement in late July of a project to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors. FRANCE 24's Selina Sykes speaks with Dr. Emanuel Macedo de Medeiros, Co-founder and Global CEO of the Sport Integrity Global Alliance.

items.title: 'A futuristic debate now very real': Why the world is struggling to regulate killer robots
items.desc: Representatives from 128 nations are meeting in Geneva on Monday to decide whether to move ahead with negotiating legally binding rules around the use of AI-powered weapons that can kill without human involvement. FRANCE 24 spoke with artificial intelligence researcher Vincent Boulanin to find out just what is at stake.

items.title: Czech mass protests: Media is the first casualty 'when you want to attack democracy'
items.desc: As hundreds of thousands of people gather in Prague to protest the Czech government's proposal to replace public broadcasting licence fees with direct state funding, Delano D'Souza is pleased to welcome Bára Stárek, Executive Director of Díky, že můžem. Stárek warns that the proposed changes offer "no real safeguards" against political influence, pointing to developments in Slovakia and Hungary. She also drew a parallel with the Velvet Revolution of 1989, recalling that "we didn't have a free media and we only had a state media" under communist rule. "Media is the first (line of) attack when you want to attack democracy," she said. With the legislation expected to reach Parliament in January, Stárek believes the demonstrations will continue if the government refuses to engage in any discussions.

items.title: Robert Pattinson: British actor will be the next James Bond
items.desc:
British actor Robert Pattinson is set to become the next James Bond in the long-running 007 spy franchise.
 
Discussions over the casting of the new James Bond had been going on for months, with Pattinson emerging as one of the frontrunners from the outset.

items.title: Russia's war on Ukraine: 'Americans want to have a deal whatever the cost for both Ukraine & Europe'
items.desc: Delano D'Souza is pleased to welcome Grégoire Roos, Director of the Europe and Russia and Eurasia Programmes at Chatham House. As European countries prepare to take part in the next round of Ukraine peace talks, Roos questions whether having five European representatives could weaken their negotiating position. "The other option is to realize that it dilutes the negotiating power of Europe. And I would lean towards that," he says, proposing Finnish President Alexander Stubb as a possible representative. Roos also points to differences between Washington and European governments over negotiations with Russia. While "the Americans do absolutely want to have a deal whatever the cost for both Ukraine and Europe," he argues that European governments have little choice but to maintain pressure on Moscow, which has yet to abandon its "maximalist demands."

items.title: Robert Pattinson named as new James Bond
items.desc: British actor ​Robert Pattinson will be the next James Bond, Amazon MGM Studios announced on Monday, ​taking on the role after Daniel Craig's departure from the long-running spy series.

items.title: French film star Depardieu drops appeal against sexual conviction
items.desc: French film star Gérard Depardieu on Monday dropped his appeal against a conviction for sexually assaulting two women during the filming of a movie in 2021 and issued "sincere apologies" for his past behaviour on set. "For a long time on film sets, I hid behind provocation and ribald humour," Depardieu, 77, said in the statement, withdrawing his appeal on the day it was set to go to trial. "I believed my remarks and some of my gestures would be without consequences" for those involved, he said. "They were not, particularly coming from a powerful figure such as I once was."

items.title: French troops in Ukraine 'wouldn't be a surprise'
items.desc: French soldiers have been operating in Ukraine for several months, training Ukrainian troops and helping maintain military equipment, France 24's sister radio network Radio France Internationale (RFI) reported on Monday. While the deployment has not been confirmed, such a mission would not come as a surprise to many in Ukraine, reports France 24's correspondent in Kyiv Gulliver Cragg.

items.title: Prague: Thousands of Czechs rally against government media funding plan
items.desc: Tens of thousands of Czechs rallied in Prague on Sunday, November 15, against a government plan to cut a public media fee and move funding to the state budget, a policy critics say would dent the broadcasters' independence and viability.

items.title: Robert Pattinson named as new James Bond
items.desc: British actor Robert Pattinson, star of three mega-franchises, "The Batman", "Harry Potter" and "Twilight", has been named as the seventh 007. The announcement ends years of speculation about who would inherit the beloved role from Daniel Craig and comes five years after the last Bond release, "No Time to Die".

items.title: Melissa Auf Der Maur: 90s rock memoirs and photographs
items.desc: Melissa Auf Der Maur grew up in Montreal, the daughter of a feminist activist mother and a journalist-turned-politician father. At just 22, she joined Courtney Love’s band Hole as its bass player, going on to become a role model for young female fans – and not only female fans – of alternative rock. She later joined The Smashing Pumpkins before striking out on her own as a solo artist. She dropped by FRANCE 24 to talk to Marjorie Hache about the epic decade that brought the 20th century to a close.

items.title: Verdict due in French trial over triple murder linked to Marseille drug wars
items.desc: In France, a highly anticipated verdict in a triple homicide is expected later today. Often called the Kessaci trial, the plight of the Kessaci family has drawn attention across France, the surviving brother Amine Kessaci has become an outspoken advocate against drug trafficking and in particular in Marseille.

items.title: Did France abandon its athletes after the Olympics?
items.desc: Two years after hosting the Olympics, France seems to have lost interest in supporting its athletes. With budget cuts and lackluster interest from sponsors, some – despite their competitive successes – are turning to influencer work to finance their sport careers.

items.title: COP31 deal draft foreshadows difficult route to consensus
items.desc: COP31 negotiators in Turkey released a draft agreement on Monday to advance talks on fossil fuels and climate finance before this week's deadline. The pressure to reach a deal is intense after a year of environmental challenges including  catastrophic glacier flooding in Nepal and European wildfires, even as global conflict and cost-of-living protests distract leaders from climate action.

items.title: Saudi Arabia dismisses commander of anti-Houthi coalition as rebels advance
items.desc: Saudi Arabia has removed the commander of the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen, state media said Monday, as the Iran-backed rebels advanced on the temporary capital of Aden. The shake up comes after Houthi forces took territory on Yemen's southern coast and Saudi-backed forces fell back to defend the capital.

items.title: 'Historical fiction is about filling in the gaps', author Ian McGuire says
items.desc: A Man Booker Prize nominee has been speaking to FRANCE 24 about his latest novel and his passion for researching and writing historical fiction. Ian McGuire was shortlisted for the prize in 2016 for his novel “The North Water”. His latest book, “White River Crossing”, was published earlier this year and has now been translated into French, under the shortened title “White River”.
